facts_to_cover: Goodbye, Lara (Sayonara, Lara) is a Kinema Citrus Summer 2026 Crunchyroll original, 12 episodes, airing Sundays.

Premise is a Little Mermaid inversion: mermaid princess Lara becomes human for a prince, is rejected when her tail bursts in front of him, dissolves into sea foam and dies in Episode 1, then reincarnates 200 years later in modern Kyoto.
Modern-day cast: her witch aunt Grace is reincarnated as a talking pet fish; national-level boxer Mari Ootsu takes Lara in.

New character Luca is introduced in Episode 7 (aired Aug 16-17, 2026) and gives Lara emotional closure from her original prince-rejection trauma, telling her he likes her 'because she's just herself.'
Episode 7 ends with Lara and Luca on a fireworks date, followed by an end-credits sequence showing Lara dissolving into sea foam again -- the exact fate that killed her in Episode 1.
Episode 4 (aired 2026-07-28) had already built foreshadowing that boxer Mari, not a new love interest, is set up as Lara's true emotional match, per Anime News Network's review.
Real fan debate is happening now (Reddit thread dated Aug 17, 2026) over whether Luca is a genuine love interest or a narrative red herring given the foam-again end card.

The angle: the show just used its own signature death imagery (sea foam) as a coded 'wrong answer' signal right after introducing Luca -- viewers cheering for Luca may be falling for the same setup that killed Lara once already.

After their kiss goes viral, Arata becomes an unwilling celebrity, and the two try to avoid being seen together. They meet anyway, hiding in a festival crowd, but the crowd separates them. This time it's not love that triggers her transformation — it's the panic of being alone. Arata calms her down, and they reunite for the fireworks. A published review calls this the first time her trigger wasn't romantic. Is the show quietly rewriting its own rule? Leave your take.

facts_to_cover: Kaiju Girl Caramelise (Otome Kaiju Caramelize) is a Liden Films Summer 2026 anime based on Spica Aoki's manga, airing on Crunchyroll (Japan broadcast Fridays on TBS/BS11/AT-X), premiered July 3, 2026.

Premise: high schooler Kuroe Akaishi has a rare condition that causes her to transform into a giant kaiju (Harugon) whenever overwhelming emotion -- especially romantic feeling for classmate Arata Minami -- takes over.
In Episode 6 ('Rairi's Forest,' aired Aug 7, 2026), Kuroe kisses Arata while transformed as Harugon; video of it goes viral and Arata is dubbed the 'Prince of Kaiju.'
Episode 7 ('All Eyes on Arata,' aired Aug 14, 2026) opens with Arata now an unwilling celebrity because of that viral video, and the two have to hide their relationship from paparazzi and the public.

At a fireworks festival together, Kuroe and Arata get separated by the crowd -- and the STRESS of being alone and missing the fireworks, not romantic feeling, is what triggers her transformation into Harugon this time.

Anime News Network's Episode 7 review (published Aug 17, 2026) explicitly flags this as a first: 'I believe this is a first, as it is not her crush on Minami that triggers it, but rather her despair at being alone.'

The review also reframes this transformation as a defensive/protective retreat rather than a loss of control -- the crowd leaves her alone once she's a kaiju, which lets her and Arata reunite for the fireworks finale.
Episode 7 ends on a post-credits stinger: obsessive friend Manatsu is shown waiting at Arata's house dressed as Harugon, setting up a jealousy-driven complication next episode.

The angle: this show has spent 6 episodes training viewers that Kuroe transforms because of romantic overload, and Episode 7 just quietly broke that rule without any characters (or most viewers) noticing the shift.
